🇳🇵 LOCAL SURVIVORS OF THE NEPAL FLOODS: THEY SURVIVED, BUT LOST ALMOST EVERYTHING For many local people, surviving the devastating floods was only the beginning of another struggle. 73-year-old Bhakta Lal Shrestha was at an elderly home in Devighat when the flood struck. He and more than 100 other residents were trapped for nearly nine hours before rescuers finally reached them. In Tupche village, 49-year-old Parbati Adhikari survived because she had left her village to visit a nearby temple before the flood arrived. When she tried to return, five bridges had already been washed away. She eventually found shelter with other survivors and was reunited with her husband and son. And 8-year-old Zoyal Ghale survived by running into the forest and climbing trees as floodwaters tore through his community. Injured and alone, he was eventually rescued and later reunited with his mother. These are more than numbers. They are mothers, fathers, children, grandparents and entire families who watched their homes disappear in minutes. Some survived. Some are still missing. One mystery is how so much water got mobilized into the flood. Some researchers initially suggested a glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF), in which the “liquid concrete–like slurry” of the fallen mountainside formed a temporary dam on the Lhende Khola, then rapidly released millions of cubic meters of water when the dam burst. But the seismic and satellite data show “absolutely no evidence” of a GLOF. A scientist suggests the flow of rock, ice, and sediment scooped up river water as it rushed downstream. Nepal has been hit by a catastrophic flash flood disaster, beginning on 26 August 2026, particularly along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river corridors. 🇳🇵 What happened? The flooding was not simply ordinary monsoon flooding. A sudden ice/rock avalanche and collapse in the Himalayan region near Tibet caused a huge surge of water, mud, rocks and debris into the Bhote Koshi River. The resulting flash flood swept through villages and infrastructure with very little warning.  The worst-affected areas include Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and Chitwan, with impacts also reported in Gorkha and Tanahun.  🕯️ Deaths and missing people The situation has continued to worsen as rescue teams recover bodies and update missing-person lists. As of 29–30 August, reports indicate more than 600 people have died in Nepal, with thousands still missing across Nepal and Tibet. AP reported 669 deaths in Nepal and nearly 3,000 people still missing as of August 30.  Many of the missing include foreign nationals, tourists, pilgrims and workers. 🚨 Rescue operation Nepalese security forces, helicopters and emergency teams are continuing search-and-rescue operations. More than 3,700 people have reportedly been rescued, while difficult mountain terrain, damaged roads and unstable conditions are making the operation extremely difficult.  A temporary lake formed near the disaster area also created fears of another flood, although the immediate risk has reportedly decreased as the lake has begun draining.  💔 Damage The floods have destroyed or severely damaged: Homes and entire villages Roads and bridges Hydropower plants Electricity infrastructure Border/trade infrastructure Health facilities Tourist and pilgrimage routes Nepal's government estimates that rebuilding could cost approximately US$4–5 billion. A sudden ice/rock avalanche and collapse in the Himalayan region near Tibet caused a huge surge of water, mud, rocks and debris into the Bhote Koshi River. The resulting flash flood swept through villages and infrastructure with very little warning.  The worst-affected areas include Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and Chitwan, with impacts also reported in Gorkha and Tanahun.  🕯️ Deaths and missing people The situation has continued to worsen as rescue teams recover bodies and update missing-person lists. More than 3,700 people have reportedly been rescued, while difficult mountain terrain, damaged roads and unstable conditions are making the operation extremely difficult.
